@twoertwein There is one more decision I’d like to consult you about: Currently the ORC writer in pyarrow doesn’t handle dictionary type which correspond to categorical type in pandas.

Hence for dataframes with one or more categorical columns we probably need to do one of the following:
1. Raise ValueError and explain the issue in Arrow.
2. Convert categorical columns into string / object columns before proceeding. Maybe we can warn users about the issue.

On the Arrow side I can get dictionary type enabled in the ORC writer in 9.0.0 if necessary. However given our release schedules it will likely be slightly after the next Pandas release.

Since Pandas needs backward compatibility the choice we make here is likely to remain until 2.0.0. Which one do you think is more appropriate? Personally I’m inclined towards 2 since categorical columns are quite common and that it is quite natural to change the behavior once we improve other typing-related aspects of Pandas according to the roadmap such as adding string type and making null handling consistent.

issue_context.title: ENH: to_orc
issue_context.body:
Hello,

Is it possible to add to_orc method to pandas.DataFrame, from pyarrow 4.0.0 ?

Br
Nicolas
comments: @NickFillot Note that pyarrow 4.0.0 and pyarrow 4.0.1+ have different orderings in the ORC writer. I think we should use the latest one which is in line with the Parquet writer of Arrow.

review_comments: can you add a versionadded 1.5 tag
Sure! Done!
Do you expect that there will be multiple pyarrow-like modules? If not, you can probably remove this argument.
Yes. There is also `pyorc` which can also read and write ORC files. I can add it once this PR is merged.
same here
Fixed!
Did you push your changes?
How is `None` handled?
Good catch! It has been fixed.
You are welcome to add overloads here as well but would be less important.
Nit: Could you move the `pd.DataFrame` call to the test where you are using this list since it's common among all these arguments?
Sure!
@mroeschke The last one has extra transformation after it became a dataframe so we can't really just move the call to the test.

Will pyarrow raise if these dtypes are passed? If so, can a a pyarrow error be caught and reraised as a `NotImplementedError` so this can be more flexible to other potential dtypes not supported in the future?
I need to test these types individually. Not sure right now.
@mroeschke  It seg faults out for all instances but sparse. I need to catch them in Arrow 9.0.0. Meanwhile can we use the current dtype filter?

Okay, this is fine then given:

1. Could you use the type checking functions in `pandas.core.dtypes.common` instead? e.g. `is_categorical_dtype(dtype)`?
2. Could you make a note that in pyarrow 9.0.0 this checking should not be needed?
Sure!

Done!

Since for sparse dtypes we get a `TypeError` from Arrow when converting the dataframe to a pyarrow table I plan to use `TypeError` for the other 4 in pyarrow 9.0.0 as well. The try-except block has been added in addition to the type checks for the 4 that segfault out right now with the note.
